parsed.basis: Botswana has no criminal offence covering transgender identity or expression, and consensual same-sex conduct was upheld as lawful by the Court of Appeal in 2021, with the relevant Penal Code paragraphs formally deleted in 2026. High Court rulings in 2017 required recognition of transgender people's gender identity on identity documents, although no clear administrative process for legal gender recognition had been introduced by 2023. No documented pattern of violence against transgender visitors is recorded, while societal discrimination has been reported and tolerance measures remain divided. LEGABIBO is legally registered and provides support resources. No region-specific information distinguishes North-West District from the national picture.
